h1: Powder Coat Stripping and Recoating for Metal Parts
byline: By the Koojo Custom Powder Coating production team | Updated 14 October 2026

blocks.text: Powder coat stripping and recoating removes a failed, damaged or unwanted finish and replaces it with a fresh powder coat finish that bonds to clean metal. At Koojo Custom Powder Coating in Milton, we have finished more than 10,000 items since 2012, and many of them were older parts brought back into service. Whether your railings are peeling, your frames are chipped or your equipment has rusted, our powder coat removal and recoating service restores the metal and its protection. Tell us what the part is and what is wrong with it, and we will recommend the right approach.

Our standard turnaround is 48 hours for typical shop orders, and we are open Monday to Friday, 7 AM to 5 PM. Heavily rusted or multi-part jobs are scheduled when we quote, once we know the size, the condition and how much old coating removal the parts need. Every powder coat stripping and recoating job starts with a short conversation about the part and what went wrong.

What Is Powder Coat Stripping and Recoating?

Powder coat stripping and recoating is a two-part restoration process. The old finish comes off completely, then new powder is applied electrostatically and cured in an oven. The goal is a clean, even finish that bonds to bare metal instead of a new layer sitting on a failing one.

Powder coat recoating over a damaged finish rarely lasts. A peeling powder coat or a chipped powder coating usually means the bond has already failed, and a new coat on top can lift in the same places. Rust under the surface makes this worse, because it keeps spreading beneath any new film. That is why we remove the old finish first and complete surface rust treatment before the new powder goes on.

Not every part needs full powder coating restoration. A faded powder coat on a sound surface may only need cleaning and a refresh, while rust, damage or a colour change calls for complete old coating removal. We assess each part before we quote, so powder coat stripping and recoating covers only the work the part actually needs.
How Our Powder Coat Stripping and Recoating Process Works

Our powder coat stripping and recoating process has six stages: assessment, removal, rust repair, pretreatment, recoating and inspection. Each stage protects the next one, so the new finish bonds properly and lasts.

items: Assessment. We look at the metal, the existing coating, the extent of rust and any damage. Photos sent with your quote request help us plan the stripping and recoating, including the removal method, the repairs and the finish, before the part arrives.

Removal. We take the old finish down to bare metal. Paint stripping and powder coat stripping take different effort, so we confirm the method for your part when we quote. Heavy coatings, scale and rust often call for blasting, described on our [sandblasting services](/services/sandblasting) page.

Rust repair. Surface rust is cleaned from the metal so it cannot spread under the new coat. Deep pitting or structural damage is flagged to you early, because recoating cannot restore a weakened part.

Pretreatment. Clean metal can develop flash rust quickly, so pretreatment before recoating follows removal closely. Our [surface preparation](/services/surface-preparation) page explains the washing and masking steps, and surface preparation for recoating is part of every restoration job.
Recoating. We plug threads and bores, then apply the powder electrostatically. Oven curing at 180–200 °C melts the powder into one continuous film.
Inspection. We check coverage, colour and finish, measure film thickness and look for defects before packing the part.

blocks.text: Timing matters as much as technique. Typical shop work follows our standard 48-hour turnaround, and we receive parts Monday to Friday, 7 AM to 5 PM. Planning powder coat stripping and recoating as one job keeps bare metal from sitting uncoated, which is the main cause of early flash rust. Recoating turnaround for larger or heavily rusted parts is confirmed when we quote. Parts with several layers of old paint can take longer to strip, so we ask for photos early.
Which Parts and Metals Can We Restore?

Our stripping and recoating service covers steel and aluminum parts that can withstand curing, from small brackets to large fabricated frames. See our [capabilities](/capabilities) page for size and weight limits. Typical jobs include:

items: Railings and gates. Railing restoration and gate restoration are common, because outdoor metalwork loses its finish first.
Equipment and machinery. Equipment refurbishment and machinery refurbishment bring worn housings, guards and frames back to a protected finish.
Structural steel and frames. Structural steel recoating suits fabricated frames and supports where rust has started under the old coat.
Older metalwork. Aging metalwork from churches, parks and buildings often carries several layers of old paint, which we remove before recoating.

blocks.text: Galvanized, cast and heavily welded parts can need extra checks because trapped gases may affect the surface, so tell us the material when you request a quote. Some parts are not worth restoring, and we will say so if the metal is too weak or too damaged. For parts that live outdoors, powder coat stripping and recoating helps restore weathered metal and extend coating life.
Restoration and Recoating Options
You can return a part to its original look or change it completely. The stripping and recoating options below cover the most common requests, and each can be paired with a new finish.

items: Like-for-like recoating. We aim for an original colour match so the restored part blends with the rest of the installation. Send a colour code, a RAL number or a small sample.
Colour change recoating. A new shade, sheen or texture gives older parts a new look. Our [custom powder coating colours](/services/custom-colors-finishes) page explains the choices.
Removal with repair. Some parts need old coating removal and rust repair before they return to service. Tell us what is wrong and we will confirm the steps.
Repair or recoat. A small chip may be repairable, but widespread peeling, rust or fading means a full recoat is the better choice. We tell you which applies when we assess the part.

blocks.text: Not sure whether your part needs stripping at all? Send photos with your quote request. A restoration quote for powder coat stripping and recoating starts with a clear description of the damage and the finish you want, and it lets us refinish metal parts without guesswork. Whatever you choose, we confirm the plan with you before work starts.
How We Check Restoration Quality

For every powder coat stripping and recoating job, we check the bare metal after removal, then the finished coat, before parts leave the shop. Our quality steps are outlined on our [certification](/certification) page, and test reports are available on request.

Where a job calls for it, test methods include the ASTM D3359 adhesion test, ASTM D7091 for dry film thickness and ASTM B117 for salt spray resistance. Our certification is held through the Absolute Bureau of Certification. A new finish is only worth applying if it stays bonded, so we test adhesion as well as appearance on powder coat recoating work, which helps prevent a repeat adhesion failure or coating failure. We also confirm the cured finish is even, with no thin spots, runs or bare patches.

Municipal and institutional owners, contractors, farm and heavy equipment owners and manufacturers use our powder coat stripping and recoating service most. These customers have metal that has aged, and they need a durable finish back quickly, with a clear scope and a documented result.

Our powder coat stripping and recoating also supports our wider [industrial powder coating](/services/industrial-powder-coating) work and the full range of [powder coating services](/services) at our Milton shop.
Stripping and Recoating FAQs

Short answer: powder coat stripping and recoating removes a failed finish and applies a new cured coat to clean metal. These answers cover how we recoat metal parts, from removal and rust to colour and timing, so you know what to expect before you book.

blocks.q: Can you remove old powder coating from my part?
blocks.a: Yes. Our powder coat stripping takes the finish down to bare metal, then we check the surface and recoat it. Send photos and part details with your quote request so we can confirm the removal method and any repairs.

blocks.q: Is it better to repair a chip or recoat the whole part?
blocks.a: A small chip may be repairable, but widespread chipping, peeling or rust means a full recoat is the better choice. A new coat on top of a failing one tends to lift again, so we advise stripping and recoating with a bare metal finish first.

blocks.q: Do you treat rust before recoating?
blocks.a: Yes. We clean surface rust from the metal so it cannot spread under the new coat. Deep pitting or structural damage is flagged early, because recoating cannot restore a weakened part.

blocks.q: Can I change the colour when I recoat?
blocks.a: Yes. A recoat is a good time to choose a new colour, sheen or texture. Send a RAL number or sample and we will confirm what is available when we quote.

blocks.q: How long does powder coat stripping and recoating take?
blocks.a: Typical shop orders follow our standard 48-hour turnaround. Large, heavily rusted or multi-part jobs are scheduled when we quote, once we know the size, condition and amount of removal.

blocks.q: What should I send for a restoration quote?
blocks.a: Send photos of the part, its size and quantity, a description of the problem and the colour you want. This lets us price powder coat stripping and recoating accurately.
